label: Ubiquiti UniFi Mobile Router Ultra (UMR-Ultra)
description: UniFi Mobile Router Ultra: 2x 100M RJ45, LTE Cat 4, WiFi 4, USB-C or 9-30 V DC, DIN/wall mount, no PoE.
notes: Vendor figures: **(2) FE RJ45 ports** - fast ethernet - **LTE Cat 4**, WiFi 4 1x1, **5.7 W**, USB-C 5 V/2 A or **9-30 V DC** on a 4-pin ATX header, **-30 to 70 C** operating. **The "Ultra" is the lesser unit**: against the UMR it drops both ports from gigabit to 100M, loses PoE entirely, and gives up LTE band coverage - in exchange for a wider DC input range, a wider temperature range and one third less power. The name does not rank the hardware. **Cited 2026-11-19.** Every figure from https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/integrations/umr-ultra-us (200, 682,619 B): "Networking Interface (2) FE RJ45 ports, LTE Cat 4 radio, WiFi 4", "Max. Power Consumption 5.7W", "Power Method USB Type-C (5V DC/2A), 4-pin ATX DC (9-30V DC)", "-30 to 70 C", and a Features table that carries no PoE row at all. Its store page https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/umr-ultra-us (307 to its collection URL, 200 there at 587,964 B) is the second vendor surface. No datasheet exists: dl.ui.com/ds/umr-ultra_ds.pdf and dl.ui.com/ds/umr-ultra-us_ds.pdf both answer the 609,911-byte techspecs front page instead of a PDF - the silent fallback already trapped for ucg-fiber and ux-pro. The bare store slug /products/umr-ultra 307s to the internet-solutions category rather than a product, so the -us suffix is required on both hosts, the same shape as umr-us.
